entry.title: Science Based isn’t so Based
entry.content:
Science based lifting has arisen as a momentus subculture in the fitness community that seeks to replace hype and aura with t-tests and randomized controlled trials.

In an ideal world, my case would be closed here. Unfortunately, we do not live in that universe.

At the forefront of the movement are Dr. Mike Israetel and Jeff Nippard. Both of whom have been recently embroiled in controversy. But here’s the part that everyone misses: what they discussed was never science to begin with. Science is the accumulation of data and methods to support a model of understanding.

Exercise “science” fails spectacularly at this. Most studies are brutally underfunded and consequently lack the sample sizes needed to produce significant results. In fact, these tiny studies amount to a ceremonial rain dance to summon an exercise science doctorate degree from Mt. Olympus. I claim this because when we try to probe for impact within small samples, we are essentially hunting for large effect sizes.

....

But… this is exactly what we do on an individual basis when we rotate in different exercises, supplements or other habits. So, in many cases, these studies are essentially equivalent to the anecdote of someone who tried a bunch of shit(pardon me).

Think back to when you first started a sport or lifting or any physical activity. You didn’t dissect peer reviewed papers at 3 am to conclude that lifting builds muscle. The effect size is so massive that we saw loved ones, people on TV and people on social media who transformed their bodies in relatively short spans of time from working out.

That was all the convincing most people needed. And sure enough, many of us started our journies and found ourselves waking up to bigger biceps after a matter of months.

What I mean to say here is that you are not delusional for relying on anecdotes. The cost of trying a variety of things within the realm of exercise is minimal so you are effectively free to find the exercises or routine that drives a perceived larger effect for you.

But Christian… is there any nuance to this chaotic, misbegotten world of exercise science?

Yea, unfortunately.

Exercise science is a broad catch all term that is the equivalent of a shiny pokemon in the eyes of bright-eyed young men who want like lifting and also want to go to college(ie, it’s probably a term that got popularized by some random major at some random university. Don’t quote me on this though).

That said, it encompasses things like rehabilitation or exercise physiology which are legitimate and vitally important domains. Injury management is not an area where we can feel around in the dark and hope to find the right solution. We need drumroll SCIENCE!

Science is the dull claymore that we will use to hack apart the barbarian that is injury management. The cost of failing to rehab a knee in an older patient could literally be their life 1.

As a consequence, it literally becomes necessary to approach this with science. Unfortunately, as it stands, it is still difficult to fund(think several million dollars) and perform longitudinal studies on various exercise based interventions on people with injury. A lot of existing knowledge and methods lie with experts at the time of my writing.

Bringing this back to Dr. Mike and Jeff Nippard, I believe that their bastardization of science is plainly terrible. At the same time, they and other content creators have done a good job at attempting to make exercise more accessible for the elderly and folks with chronic injury. I think that’s the area where current science based lifters actually shine despite it almost never being under the purview of social media.

The Ultimate Takeaway: it’s okay if you are not optimizing your workouts via science… because neither are they.

entry.title: On Loneliness
entry.content:
We often seek comfort in others, in connection, in validation. But the hardest paths — the ones worth walking — are lonely by nature. No one can do your push-ups for you. No one can overcome your doubts, suffer your pain, or climb your mountains…

That abomination is ChatGPT’s take on an article titled On Loneliness 😆. It’s quite frankly a far cry from the intent of this post. I’ve fortunately had the opportunity to muse about loneliness several times in the past few days. These musings occured during my vain attempts to encourage friends to be happy even without their “special someone.”

“Several” is just enough to make me standardize my thoughts and put them in one place. The next time someone complains about how looking for a partner is making them miserable, I will (hopefully) link them this instead of crashing out. With that said, if you’re one of those friends, thank you.

You got me to write again.

A Thought Experiment or Two

The concept of monks has fascinated me to no end. There are these robed, jacked guys (or gals!1) who do nothing but work out and meditate. No wives, no kids, no jobs, no YouTube, no Clash Royale.

Motivated by their way of life, I considered this thought experiment:

  1. You could never have a romantic relationship in the future.
  2. After being informed of this, you can choose to continue living or die painlessly.

Most people (whether they admit it or not) would choose to continue living. Maybe with even more passion and drive towards their friends, family, and other goals. Fewer options can actually increase satisfaction because they pull us away from the constant tug-of-war of desire.

To be clear, I am not suggesting that you shave your head and swear off sexual relations forever. This is just a proof of concept: life is still worth living, even in the unlikely “worst case.”

A similar experiment would be to imagine that you’re a heterosexual man in a world where women never existed (bear with me). In this hypothetical, you’d have nothing to miss and you’d aspire to live your best life without being moopy from lacking a partner. Maybe, just maybe, you’d even listen to love songs and think about yourself instead of the one that got away.

Here’s the point: ideally you would be happy without a relationship. If you have a deep-seated desire to form a bond and perhaps to have a family, that’s beautiful. But that shouldn’t be bringing you great anguish. Ideally, it would sting about as much as failing an interview or bombing an exam.

Crushing ANTs

Imagine scrolling reels or tiktok with no cares in the world before being jump scared by an image of slenderman… Now let’s do it again. Except you’re not scrolling reels and you’re actually trying to sleep before your big presentation tomorrow. And instead of slenderman, you suddenly remember your ex and wonder “Why wasn’t I good enough?”.

That is an Automatic Negative Thought or Ant for short.

If your desire for love is strong and unmet, it’s easy to start linking that absence with your worst fears about yourself. That’s where crushing Ants becomes essential.

Ants are disempowering. Worse they’re addictive. Instead of picking ourselves up when we’re down, we spiral. We reinforce the pain. Anything that isn’t self-love becomes self-hate.

The ability to acknowledge an Ant is one definition for mindfulness. Mindfulness is a whole other can of worms about interpretting our emotions as stimuli that call for some action blah blah blah blah(it’s actually really cool!).2

So how do we kill an ANT?

As fast as it appeared is as fast as we cut it down. But we don’t stop there. We replace the thought with its opposite.

  • “I’m never going to be the one for her and I’m pathetic for trying again and again.”
    → “Just because she isn’t the one for me doesn’t mean no one is. I’m learning, growing, and moving forward.”

  • “I’m fat, autistic, have no friends and will never find love.”
    → “I may not have the connections I want yet, but I’m capable of creating deep, meaningful relationships. I am lovable. And I will be the first to love me.”

  • “Why can’t I be normal?”
    → “My struggles are real, but they don’t make me less. I am human. I am allowed to be me.”

These are real thoughts sampled from r/kitchencels. [Check the footnote for their associated foods!]3

The ability to rewrite our narrative is very real. ANTs often sound absurd when said aloud — they’re the things we only tell ourselves when we’re most vulnerable. If a friend came to you with these thoughts, you’d never say, “You’re right, give up.”

So don’t say it to yourself.

Closing Thoughts

When you approach life from a base of happiness, the hurdles of life stay just that: hurdles. Not catastrophes. Not identity crises. Just hurdles.

It’s okay to be alone. It’s okay to feel lonely.
Just don’t let those thoughts hijack your story.

Live, breathe, and be happy.
There’ll be time to talk about dating after that.

  1. Here’s a real-life example of Buddhist nuns practicing similar lifestyles ↩

  2. You’ve probably heard of professional athletes who, when asked “Are you nervous?”, reply “I feel excited.” They’re likely feeling the same stimulus we all do — they just choose to interpret it differently. That act of interpretation is mindfulness. ↩
